title: Springfield Local School District Education: 84 Black students were enrolled in 2023-24 school year
text:
Paul Craft Ohio Superintendent of Public Instruction | https://sboe.ohio.gov/about-us/superintendent/01-superintendent
Paul Craft Ohio Superintendent of Public Instruction | https://sboe.ohio.gov/about-us/superintendent/01-superintendent
Ohio Department of Education & Workforce.
Data showed that Springfield Local School District welcomed 1,724 students during the 2023-24 school year. Among them, Black students made up 4.9% of the student body, making them the third most represented ethnicity in the district.
Springfield Local School District roughly covers four schools within Summit County and has its main office in Akron.
Among the four schools in Springfield Local School District, Spring Hill Elementary School recorded the highest enrollment of Black students in the 2023-24 school year, with a total of 40 students.
In 2022, Ohio saw an average student-to-teacher ratio of approximately 1:15, which is better than the national average of 1:16. This marks an improvement for the state, especially compared to 2016, when the ratio reached its decade-high at 16.1 students per teacher.
Despite the apparent improvement, this positive trend is overshadowed by a general decline in public school enrollments, which was accelerated by the pandemic. This decline, aligned with the steady number of teachers in the state over the last 10 years, has led to low student-to-teacher ratios.
Year | Total District Enrollment | Total Black Students | Black % |
---|---|---|---|
2023-24 | 1,724 | 84 | 4.9% |
2022-23 | 1,711 | 71 | 4.1% |
2021-22 | 1,810 | 64 | 3.5% |
